# filmopen_state

*Generated by `scripts/package_digest.py`; regenerate, never edit.*

The application's state, in Riverpod: settings (`settingsProvider`, the viewer handle, development mode, and `settingsTabProvider`, Settings' open tab), the open project (`projectProvider`: `openSample` / `openDirectory` / `createProject`, `refresh`, `saveEntity`, `fork`, `setOfficial`, `setPick`, and `addChild` / `removeChild` / `moveChild`, which add a folder or a scene to a `children` list, take an entry out of one and move one — within a list, between two (the destination first, the origin second) or out of *Not in the script* —: the entity first and the parent second, everything that can be known refused before anything is written, each file written as it was checked (a change made meanwhile is refused as stale, never absorbed), and the parent's change routed through the draft a form has open on that file), navigation (`browserProvider.navigate`, `Selection` — `ScriptSelection` for the Script page among them —, the tree model and `TreeBuilder`, `scriptOutlineProvider`, the one walk of the script that the tree and the pages read, and `ScriptRowText`, what a row of it says wherever it is drawn), launch arguments, localisation, the bundled model catalogue read once (`catalogueProvider`, the format's one reader, which Provider keys, dictation and the plug-in host share), `PageAccess` (what a page may do with the file on screen, `canRunPlugins` and `childrenLock` among it), `WriteProblemText` (the sentence for a refused write, here so that the tree and the forms both say it), and the constants the packages read.

**Flutter.** 32 files, 5,408 lines under `lib/`; 194 tests in 15 files. Barrel: `lib/filmopen_state.dart`.

## Public API

What the barrel exports, file by file. A name is `class`, `enum`, `mixin`, `extension`, `typedef`, a top-level function or variable; under a class, its public constructors, fields, getters, setters and methods.

### `lib/src/app_paths_provider.dart`

- **variable** `final preferencesLocationProvider` — The preferences file on this machine, for Settings to show; null where it is not a file the user can look at (the web, macOS and mobile).
- **variable** `final projectsInAppFolderProvider = Provider<bool>((ref)` — Whether projects live in the app's own folder — a phone — rather than in a folder the person names (milestone 5.01, D4).
- **variable** `final folderDialogsAvailableProvider = Provider<bool>((ref)` — Whether the operating system offers a folder dialog: *Open project…*, *Copy to a folder…*, the library's folder and the media folder's *Browse* are offered only where it does (milestone 5.01, D5).
- **variable** `final projectsDirectoryProvider` — Where a new project is made on a platform whose projects live in the app's own folder: the folder, created.

### `lib/src/app_version_provider.dart`

- **variable** `final appVersionProvider = Provider<String>((ref)` — The application's version, supplied by `main` from the application's own `consts.dart`, which keeps it equal to `pubspec.yaml` (`CLAUDE.md` §5).

### `lib/src/automation_host.dart`

- **class `AutomationHost`** — The seam the agent layer attaches to (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-MCP-Plan.md` §3, the refactor plan §7): what an agent may ask the running application, as an interface with a no-op default.
  - `const AutomationHost()`
  - `static AutomationHost current` — The host in use: the no-op one until [install] is called.
  - `static void install(AutomationHost host)` — Installs [host]; called by an agent entrypoint before the app's `main`.
  - `static final GlobalKey rootKey` — The `RepaintBoundary` around the page (`lib/app.dart`), so a host can take a screenshot from the render tree on every platform.
  - `static final GlobalKey windowKey` — The `RepaintBoundary` above the navigator (`lib/app.dart`'s `MaterialApp.builder`): the whole view as Flutter draws it — every route, dialog, menu, tooltip and snack bar.
  - `bool get isAvailable` — Whether this host can act at all; the no-op host cannot.
  - `void attach(ProviderContainer container)` — Called once by `main` with the container every provider lives in.
  - `Future<Map<String, Object?>> state()` — What is on screen: the open project, the selection, the tab, the viewer — as data an agent can read.
  - `Future<void> navigate(Selection selection)` — Shows [selection], as a tree click would.
  - `Future<void> setTab(String tab)` — Opens the tab named [tab] on the current page.
  - `Future<bool> tap(String identifier)` — Taps the element carrying the semantics [identifier]; false when no such element is on screen.
  - `Future<bool> setField(String stem, String key, String text)` — Types [text] into the field [key] of the form editing [stem], through the form's own setter (`FieldRegistry`), so the autosave, the identity lock and the stale refusal hold as for a person.
  - `Future<Uint8List?> screenshot()` — A PNG of the whole view ([windowKey], dialogs included), or null when the host cannot paint one.
  - `Future<Object?> semantics()` — The semantics tree as data: labels, identifiers, actions.
  - `Future<List<String>> logTail({int lines = 50})` — The last [lines] of the application's log.
  - `Future<void> openProject(String? path)` — Opens the project folder at [path], or the bundled sample when [path] is null — the project menu's two doors.
  - `Future<void> setViewer(String handle)` — Sets the viewer handle as Settings does; an empty or invalid handle browses as nobody.
  - `Future<void> setLocale(String? code)` — Chooses the language by its code (`en`, `es`) as Settings does, or the platform's language when [code] is null.
  - `Future<void> setTheme(String mode)` — Chooses the theme as Settings does: `system`, `light` or `dark`.
- **class `NoOpAutomationHost`** — The host of every product build: answers "not available" to everything and does nothing.
  - `const NoOpAutomationHost()`

### `lib/src/children_controller.dart`

- **class `AddedChild`** — **The script's three operations** — *Add folder…* / *Add scene…*, *Remove from folder*, and every move — with what they answer.
  - `const AddedChild(this.stem, {this.notListed})`

  - `final Object? notListed` — Null when the parent lists the new entry.
- **class `UnchangedChildrenException`** — A change of a `children` list that would change nothing: an entry that is not there to remove, one the list names already, a row moved to where it is.
  - `UnchangedChildrenException(this.parentStem)`

- **class `ChildrenChangedMeanwhileException`** — A list of the script is not what it was when the person asked: the file that held it is gone from the index, or the list read back is not the one intended — another write landed in between.

  - `final bool alreadyListed` — The destination named the folder or scene already — perhaps under another spelling, a pin or none — so it took no second listing and the move was the removal alone: the caller says so, since the spelling that was move…
- **extension `ChildrenController`**
  - `Future<AddedChild> addChild({ required EntityType type, required String tag, required String name, String? kind, required String parentStem, })` — *Add folder…* and *Add scene…* (milestone 5.11, the plan's §3.9): the viewer's first version of a new folder or scene, listed at the end of the `children` of the file [parentStem] — the project file the script is read…
  - `Future<void> removeChild({required String parentStem, required String entry, int occurrence = 0})` — *Remove from folder*: takes [entry] — the [occurrence]-th of that exact text — out of the `children` of [parentStem], and **deletes nothing**: the folder or scene is then under *Not in the script* (Project Specificati…
  - `Future<MovedChild> moveChild({ required String entry, String? fromStem, int occurrence = 0, required String toStem, int? index, })` — *Move up*, *Move down*, *Move to…* and a drop (milestone 5.11, the plan's §3.10): [entry] — the [occurrence]-th of that exact text in [fromStem]'s `children` — goes to [index] of [toStem]'s, or to its end.

### `lib/src/drafts.dart`

- **class `OpenDraft`** — A form's draft while its page is open: what [OpenDrafts.settleOpen] asks to be written before an action reads files as they are on disk.
  - `String get stem` — The stem of the file this is the draft of.
  - `Future<bool> settle()` — Waits for a write in flight, then writes what is pending.
  - `Map<String, dynamic>? get pending` — **The whole document this draft would write** — the file as it was read with what is typed on top — while something is pending, and **null when nothing is**, the file on disk then being what a write starts from.
  - `Future<Object?> apply(void Function(Map<String, dynamic> draft) change, {String? key, bool reseed = false})` — Takes [change] as it takes a keystroke, and writes it now: how a change made below the forms — a folder or scene added to, removed from or moved in this file's `children` (milestone 5.11), a reference or a text a job…
- **class `OpenDrafts`** — The drafts open across the app, and the writes no form waits for any more.
  - `OpenDrafts._()`
  - `static void add(OpenDraft draft)`
  - `static void remove(OpenDraft draft)`
  - `static OpenDraft? of(String stem)` — The draft open on the file [stem], if a form is: the one registered last, as the field registry answers, since two forms are on one file only while a tab slides to the next.
  - `static void track(Future<void> write)` — A write left behind, waited for by [settleDetached] until it completes.
  - `static Future<bool> settleOpen()` — Settles every draft ([OpenDraft.settle]) and waits for every write left behind, for an action that reads files the way they are on disk — a fork copies one (§13.1).
  - `static Future<void> settleDetached()` — Waits for every write **no form waits for any more** — one a form that moved to another file or went away left behind, and the write in flight of a saver disposed meanwhile — and settles no open draft.
- **class `DraftsNotSettledException`** — An open draft could not be written, so an action that writes beside it — an add, a remove, a move — did nothing: the draft's own save status says why (`OpenDrafts.settleOpen` answered false).
  - `const DraftsNotSettledException()`
- **class `DraftObserver`** — Hears every change a form's draft takes (the refactor plan §7): the entity being edited, the key that changed — or null for a change that touched several, a copy-left, a block edit — and the draft's value at that key…
  - `void onChange(Entity entity, String? key, Object? value)` — [value] is a deep copy, so an observer never writes into a draft; null when [key] is null or the change removed the key.
- **class `DraftObservers`** — The observers of every draft; empty in the product.
  - `DraftObservers._()`
  - `static void add(DraftObserver observer)`
  - `static void remove(DraftObserver observer)`
  - `static void notify(Entity entity, String? key, [Object? value])` — Tells every observer; [value] is copied once per observer, so what one does with it cannot reach another or the draft, and dropped when [key] is null.

  - `static bool setField(String stem, String key, String text)` — Types [text] into the field [key] of the form editing [stem]; false when no such form is open, when it names no such field, or when the control takes no text.

### `lib/src/page_access.dart`

- **enum `GuardNotice`** — A red line a page shows in development mode: a rule it is letting the person past, or a thing they need to know to get anywhere at all.
  - values: `otherAuthor`, `notDirector`, `libraryFile`, `noHandle`, `sessionCopy`, `readOnlyFolder`, `libraryReadOnly`, `readOnlySample`
- **enum `ChildrenLock`** — Why a version's `children` may not be changed (milestone 5.11, the plan's §3.9): what a disabled *Add folder…*, *Add scene…*, *Remove* or *Move* says, the same in the tree's menu and on a page.
  - values: `noHandle`, `readOnly`, `notYours`
- **class `PageAccess`**
  - `const PageAccess({ required this.editable, required this.canSetOfficial, required this.canLabel, required this.canRunPlugins, required this.notices…`
  - `factory PageAccess.of(FilmProject project, Entity entity, Author? viewer, Guards guards)`
  - `final bool editable` — The form writes: the viewer's own version, or — in development mode — anybody's, the shared library's included where the library can be written.
  - `final bool canSetOfficial` — The star can be pressed.
  - `final bool canLabel` — The version label can be edited.
  - `final bool canRunPlugins` — *Plugins…* may run a plug-in on the file shown: from anybody's version, since the run never writes over it.
  - `final List<GuardNotice> notices` — The red lines the page shows, in this order.
  - `final ChildrenLock? childrenLock` — Why this version's `children` may not be changed — nothing added to it, removed from it or moved in it; null when it may.
  - `bool get canEditChildren` — Whether a folder or scene may be added to, removed from or moved in this version's `children`.

  - `Future<PluginCallOutcome> call(String hook, Map<String, Object?> args, {Entity? source, PluginCallControl? control})` — Calls a platform hook through the plug-in chosen for the model asked for (milestone 5-2b §3.4): `render` with `{model, prompt, inputs, params}` for [source] — the one call *Generate* makes (the architecture's test, D8).

  - `Future<void> devClose(String stem)` — Forgets what the page wrote for [stem]: its `last-run.json`.
  - `List<PluginDevFolderProblem> get devFolderProblems` — The development folder's plug-in folders that could not be read, each with its path (milestone 5-2b §3.6): every other plug-in of the folder is there as before.
- **class `PluginRuntime`** — The seam plug-ins attach to (milestone 5.1 plan §6, D12): what the app's pages, Settings → Plugins, Provider keys and the agent layer may ask of the plug-in runtime, as an interface with a no-op default, as [Automatio…

  - `final List<PluginField> machineFields`
  - `final List<PluginAction> actions`
  - `final List<PluginProblemInfo> problems`
  - `final int linesNotWritten` — How many `ctx.log` lines of this plug-in were a sentence rather than an event name, and so went to no file (milestone 5-2 §3.6): its page says the count, so a developer whose lines are missing is told where to read them.
  - `final String? readme`
- **class `PluginDevPlugin`** — A plug-in as the developer page shows it (milestone 5-2 §3.6).
  - `const PluginDevPlugin({ required this.summary, required this.functions, required this.problems, required this.isStockCopy, required this.lastRunPat…`

  - `final List<PluginDevFunction> functions` — What it exposes, in the order the page offers them.
  - `final List<PluginProblemInfo> problems` — Every problem its files have, by the file it concerns: a developer reads them here rather than on the plug-in's own page.
  - `final bool isStockCopy` — Its files are a stock plug-in's installed copy, which the app replaces when it starts: the page says to work on a copy, or in the development folder.
  - `final String lastRunPath` — Where the last run is written, and the developer's own log: paths a person opens and an agent reads.
  - `final String logPath`
- **class `PluginDevFunction`** — One function the developer page offers to call.
  - `const PluginDevFunction({required this.name, required this.label, required this.kind, this.example})`
  - `final String name` — The function of the plug-in's object.
  - `final String label` — What to show in the pull-down: its words where it has any, else its name.
  - `final String kind` — `action`, `hook`, `offer` — or `other`, the name a person typed.
  - `final Object? example` — The arguments to fill the box with: the manifest's `example` for an offer or an action, the hook's own shape for a hook.
- **class `PluginDevRun`** — One run made from the developer page.
  - `const PluginDevRun({ required this.outcome, required this.elapsed, required this.lines, required this.lastRunPath, this.mode = PluginDevMode.app, t…`
  - `final PluginCallOutcome outcome`
  - `final Duration elapsed`
  - `final PluginDevMode mode` — How it was called, and what the function was called with — the request as sent, which in [PluginDevMode.app] is the one the app prepared.
  - `final Object? request`
  - `final List<PluginDevLine> lines` — Every `ctx.log` line of the call and a row per door it used, in order.
  - `final String lastRunPath` — Where this run was written, for a person to open and an agent to read.
- **class `PluginDevLine`** — One line of the developer page's log: a `ctx.log` the code made, or a door it used.
  - `const PluginDevLine({ required this.at, required this.kind, required this.message, this.data, this.detail, this.milliseconds, this.by, })`
  - `final int at` — Milliseconds since the run began, so a reader sees what took the time.
  - `final String kind` — The line holds what crossed into JavaScript: **no key the app holds**, and a request named by its setting or key and its route.
  - `final String message` — What the code said, or what the door was asked for.
  - `final String? data` — The JSON the code passed, or the door's answer, cut at 64 KB with a mark.
  - `final String? detail` — A door's own summary: a status, a size, a refusal's reason.
  - `final String? by` — The tag of the plug-in that made this line, where it is **not** the one the page ran: a call reaches another plug-in's code, and its lines and its doors are in this log too — a reader must see whose they are.
  - `final int? milliseconds` — How long a door took, where it waited.
- **class `PluginOffer`** — One function a plug-in offers, in its own words.
  - `const PluginOffer({required this.name, required this.label, this.help, this.example})`
  - `final String name`
  - `final String label` — The offering plug-in's words for it, in the app's language.
  - `final String? help`
  - `final Object? example` — A value of the arguments it takes, for a reader and for the developer page's argument box.
- **class `PluginCalls`** — The calls one plug-in declares on another, as consent lists them: the plug-in called, and each function **in that plug-in's words**.

  - `final String tag`
  - `final String name` — The called plug-in's name, or its tag where it is not installed.
  - `final List<String> labels` — What each called function does, in the words of the plug-in that owns it; the function's name where its manifest gives none.
  - `final bool installed` — False where the plug-in called is not installed: the page then says so, and every call answers `noProvider`.
  - `final List<String> keyPlatforms` — The platforms, by their names, of the keys the called plug-in **owns** (milestone 5-2b §3.7): a function it runs for the caller runs as its owner and may spend any of them, which consent says in the app's own words —…
- **class `PluginServer`** — A `server` setting as consent names it: the address a person types on the plug-in's page, and the default it starts with where there is one.
  - `const PluginServer({required this.key, required this.label, this.defaultAddress})`
  - `final String key`
  - `final String label` — The setting's words in the app's language.
  - `final String? defaultAddress` — The address it starts with, which can only ever be this computer.
- **class `PluginKeySlot`** — One card of Provider keys.

  - `final String keyId` — `<owner>:<slot>`.
  - `final String slot`
  - `final String platform`
  - `final String? label`
  - `final String? help`
  - `String get storeName` — The credential store's name for it (plan §3.5).
  - `String get preferenceName` — The preference that holds its state.

  - `const PluginKeyOwner({required this.owner, required this.name, required this.slots})`
  - `final String owner` — `app` or a plug-in's tag.

  - `final List<PluginKeySlot> slots`
- **class `PluginInterface`** — One interface a plug-in implements (`implements`, §14.4; milestone 5-2b §3.2), as a page lists it: its name, the platform it named where the interface asks for one, and the catalogue entries it speaks for.
  - `const PluginInterface({required this.name, this.platform, this.platformName, this.models = const []})`
  - `final String name` — `render`, `text`, `platform`, `transform`, …
  - `final String? platform` — The platform's id, where the interface asks for one.
  - `final String? platformName` — The platform file's name for it (*fal*), where one is known.
  - `final List<String> models` — The catalogue entries it speaks for; empty is *any on that platform*.
- **class `PluginProvider`** — A plug-in that provides a hook, and for which platform.
  - `const PluginProvider({required this.tag, required this.name, required this.hook, this.platform, this.platformName, this.preferred = false})`
  - `final String tag`
  - `final String name`
  - `final String hook`
  - `final String? platform`
  - `final String? platformName` — The platform file's name for [platform] (*OpenRouter*), where one is known.

- **class `PluginCallControl`** — Progress and cancellation of a running call (plan §3.4), shared by the page that started it.
  - `final progress`

  - `void cancel()`
- **class `PluginCallOutcome`** — What a call came to.
  - `const PluginCallOutcome()`
  - `PluginCallOutcomeWords get words` — What `labels.dart`'s `pluginOutcomeText` reads of this outcome (milestone 5-2c §3.6).
- **class `PluginCallDone`** — A call's value, and what it wrote: new versions' stems, takes' names.
  - `const PluginCallDone({this.value, this.message, this.messageText, this.written = const []})`
  - `final Object? value`

  - `final String? messageText`
  - `final List<String> written`
- **class `PluginCallFailed`** — Why a call has no value: `failed` (with the plug-in's own [message]), `limit` ([reason]: time, memory, stack, result, wall), `cancelled`, `hung`, `refused` ([reason]), `disabled`, `noProvider`, `notAvailable`, `stale`.
  - `const PluginCallFailed(this.code, {this.reason, this.message, this.file, this.line, this.column, this.path})`
  - `final String code`
  - `final String? reason`
  - `final String? message`
  - `final String? path` — Where an answer failed the contract, in the answer's own terms — `outputs[0].mime` — for the code `badResult` (milestone 5-2b §3.1).
  - `final String? file` — The plug-in's own code file the failure came from, and the place in it.
  - `final int? line`
  - `final int? column`
  - `String? get at` — `file:line:column`, or null where there is no position: what a page and the developer page show after the message.
- **enum `PluginStatusState`** — The four states a plug-in's `status` may answer (§14.4; milestone 5-2b §3.2): whether it can do its work now, in words a person can act on.
  - values: `ready`, `unconfigured`, `unavailable`, `degraded`
  - `static PluginStatusState? byName(String name)`

  - `const PluginCheckResult()`

  - `const PluginChecked(this.state, {this.message})`
  - `final PluginStatusState state`
  - `final String? message` — The plug-in's own message, in the person's language, where it gave one.
- **class `PluginSaysNothing`** — **The plug-in's code has no `status`**, which api 1 asks of every plug-in: its page says so, and its other functions still run — no app can know a function is missing before it has run the code.
  - `const PluginSaysNothing()`
- **class `PluginCheckFailed`** — The check did not finish: the call's own outcome.
  - `const PluginCheckFailed(this.failure)`
  - `final PluginCallFailed failure`
- **class `PluginKeyCheck`** — A plug-in's answer about a candidate key.
  - `const PluginKeyCheck({required this.accepted, this.message, this.code})`
  - `final bool accepted`
  - `final String? message` — The plug-in's own words, shown under the key's boxes.
  - `final String? code` — Where the check itself failed: the call's code.

  - `const PluginInstallOutcome({this.stem, this.refused, this.field})`
  - `final String? stem` — The installed plug-in, which then asks for consent.
  - `final String? refused` — A problem's code when the zip was refused.
  - `final String? field`

  - `const NoPluginRuntime()`

### `lib/src/project_provider.dart`

- **variable** `const AssetProjectSource bundledLibrary` — The bundled seed of the shared library, read in place where the app has no files of its own (the web).
- **variable** `final libraryProvider` — The shared library of models, platforms and plugins (§14.5): the folder the user chose in Settings; else the app's own library folder, seeded from the bundled copy on first run; else, without a disk, the bundled copy…
- **variable** `final projectProvider` — The opened project.
- **variable** `final projectClosedProvider` — Whether the person closed the project (milestone 4.6, item 13): the page then shows no project until one is opened or created.
- **class `ProjectClosedController`**
  - `void set(bool closed)`
- **variable** `final projectSourceKeyProvider` — Identifies *which* source is open, as opposed to its current contents: a re-read after a save keeps the same key, opening another folder changes it.
- **class `CreatedProject`** — What *New project* made (milestone 5.11, the plan's §3.13): the project file and the scene the script starts with, which the app opens — a person who starts a project came with a scene in mind.
  - `const CreatedProject({required this.project, required this.scene})`
  - `final VersionStem project`
  - `final VersionStem scene`
- **class `ProjectNotOpenException`** — A change was asked for in a film that is not the one open now (milestone 5-2d, the plan's §3.2): a job begun in one film and ending after another was opened, or after *Close project*.
  - `const ProjectNotOpenException(this.projectKey)`
  - `final String projectKey` — The film the change was asked for in (§5.15's `projectKeyOf`).
- **class `EntityChangedMeanwhileException`** — The file a change was for is not what it was when the change was asked for: gone from the index, or read back without the change in it (milestone 5-2d, the plan's §3.2).
  - `const EntityChangedMeanwhileException(this.stem)`
  - `final String stem`
- **class `ProjectController`**
  - `FilmProject? get baseIndex` — [_base], read-only, so a test can see that an overtaken re-read left it alone.
  - `static bool sampleOpensAsSessionCopy({required bool diskAvailable, required Guards guards})` — Whether the bundled sample opens as a session copy rather than read in place: always (milestone 4.6, items 9 and 10).
  - `Future<String> copySessionTo(String parentPath)` — *Copy to a folder…* (§9.5): writes the open session copy — every text file it holds — into a new folder `<parentPath>/<project name>`, then opens the project there, so the session's edits are kept.
  - `Future<void> openSample()`
  - `Future<void> close()` — *Close project* (milestone 4.6, item 13): every open draft is written first, then the page shows no project.
  - `Future<void> openDirectory(String path)` — Opens a folder on disk.
  - `Future<CreatedProject> createProject({ required String parentPath, required String tag, required Author author, String? name, required String epoch…` — Creates a project — `<parentPath>/<tag>/` on disk where folders can be made, else a session-only project in memory — writes its manifest (§4.4) and the creator's first `pj` version (§8), and opens it.
  - `Future<bool> refresh()` — Re-reads the current source, picking up files changed on disk.
  - `Future<void> selectProject(String stem)` — Answers the project chooser (§4.1) with one of the candidates.
  - `Future<Entity?> saveEntity(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json)` — Saves the viewer's own version with new content, then re-reads.
  - `Future<Object?> patchEntity(String projectKey, String stem, Map<String, dynamic> Function(Map<String, dynamic> json) change, { required Author? vie…` — **The one door a change made below the forms goes through** (milestone 5-2d, the plan's §3.2): a job's reference or text, and the script's own lists, which are [_changeChildren] on top of this.
  - `Future<VersionStem> createEntity({ required EntityType type, required String tag, String? epoch, required String name, String? kind, })` — A new character or location as the viewer's v1 at [epoch] (`ProjectWriter.createEntity`, milestone 4.7), then re-reads.
  - `Future<VersionStem> fork(Entity entity)` — Forks [entity] for the viewer (§13.1), re-reads, and returns the new stem so the caller can show it.
  - `Future<bool> setOfficial(Entity entity, {required bool official})` — Makes [entity] official (§13.2), or clears the pointer when [official] is false.
  - `Future<void> setPick(Entity entity)` — Makes [entity] the viewer's pick (§13.4): the version used from now on.
  - `Future<bool> abandonPick(Entity entity)` — Abandons the viewer's pick at [entity]'s epoch: it is removed, and the viewer is back on official (§13.4).
  - `Future<bool> keepPick(Entity entity)` — Keeps the viewer's pick where it is, re-dating it, so an official chosen earlier no longer supersedes it (§13.2).

### `lib/src/script_row_text.dart`

- **class `ScriptRowText`** — What a row of the script says, wherever it is drawn — the tree's Script branch, the Script page and a folder's contents (milestone 5.11, the plan's §3.7, §3.8) — so that the three read alike: the row's words, the page…
  - `const ScriptRowText({required this.label, this.detail, this.tooltip, this.shortName, this.selection, this.hasProblem = false})`
  - `final String label` — Name first, as the library's rows are: the entity's name, or the entry as it is written where it names nothing a reader can draw.
  - `final String? detail` — A folder's kind in words, a scene's short name — or the reason the row is flagged.
  - `final String? tooltip` — The stem, since the row shows the name; a longer reason for a cycle.
  - `final String? shortName` — A folder's short name, which its row shows nowhere: for a filter *by name or tag*.
  - `final Selection? selection` — The page the row opens; null for an entry that names nothing the project has.
  - `final bool hasProblem`
  - `factory ScriptRowText.of(AppLocalizations l10n, ScriptRow row)` — The words for [row].
- **function** `String? folderKindDetail(AppLocalizations l10n, Entity folder)` — A folder's kind in words: the vocabulary's in the reader's language and in lower case, as every detail of the tree is; another token **as written**, since it is the author's word and not the app's to restyle; nothing…

### `lib/src/semantics_walk.dart`

- **function** `SemanticsOwner? semanticsOwnerOf(FlutterView view)` — The semantics owner of [view]'s render view — each view has a pipeline of its own.
- **function** `bool walkSemantics(SemanticsNode node, bool Function(SemanticsNode node) visit)` — Visits [node] and its descendants depth-first, in the tree's child order, until [visit] answers false; answers whether the walk went to the end.
- **function** `SemanticsNode? findByIdentifier(SemanticsNode root, String identifier)` — The first node, in walk order, whose identifier is [identifier].
- **function** `String firstLine(String label)` — A label's first line: a tab's label carries its position ("Tab 3 of 5") on the line below its text.
- **function** `List<SemanticsNode> findByLabel(SemanticsNode root, String label)` — The nodes whose label, or whose label's first line, is [label], in walk order.
- **function** `List<SemanticsNode> tabNodes(SemanticsNode root)` — The tabs of every tab bar on screen, in order: below a node whose role is [SemanticsRole.tabBar], each node that merges one tab into itself — the node carrying the tab's label, its selection, its tooltip and its tap,…
- **function** `SemanticsAction? activationOf(SemanticsData data)` — What a click on a node does, as a screen reader asks for it: `tap`; or, where the control offers none, `expand` or `collapse` — a `DropdownMenu` (Flutter 3.47) exposes its field as a read-only text field that expands…
- **function** `SemanticsNode? nodeToTap(SemanticsNode node)` — The node a tap on [node] acts on: [node] itself when it takes a tap; else the first node below it that does — a `Semantics` wrapper above a button; else the nearest node above it that does — an identifier inside a men…
- **function** `Rect globalRect(SemanticsNode node, double devicePixelRatio)` — Where [node] is on the view, in logical pixels: its rect carried through its own transform and every ancestor's, which end in the view's [devicePixelRatio] (the root view's transform), then divided by it.
- **variable** `const List<String> valueIdentifiers` — The identifiers under which a **value** travels — what a person typed into a text field, and the two paths the developer page shows, which are selectable text and so carry a value of their own: the fields of a project…
- **function** `String maskEmailAddresses(String text)` — [text] with every e-mail address in it replaced by `<e-mail>`: how a text that can quote one travels (§3.6, D4).
- **function** `Map<String, Object?> semanticsToData(SemanticsNode node, {required double devicePixelRatio, String? identifierAbove})` — [node] and everything below it as data (§3.3): its id; its identifier, role, label, value, hint and tooltip where they are not empty; the flags that matter; the actions it takes, by name; its rect on the view in logic…
- **function** `Future<void> settleFrames({Duration timeout = const Duration(seconds: 5)})` — Waits for the frame that shows what a change did, then for the animations it started — a tab sliding, a dialog fading in — for at most [timeout].
- **function** `Future<void> nextFrame()` — The end of the next frame, scheduling one.
- **function** `Map<String, String> tabIdsOf(AppLocalizations l10n)` — The tab ids by the label each wears in [l10n] (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-MCP-Plan.md` §3.4): an entity page's — the data tab is *View* or *Edit*, whichever the page decided — and Settings' four, *General*, *Provider keys…
- **function** `String? currentTab(SemanticsNode root, AppLocalizations l10n)` — The id of the selected tab, an entity page's or Settings', or null when no tab bar is on screen.
- **class `SemanticsHit`** — What a pointer at a point reaches, as the issue recorder names it (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-Issue Recorder.md` §3.2, §4.4).
  - `const SemanticsHit({ this.identifier, this.label, this.tooltip, this.within, required this.role, this.action, this.rect, this.reachedByLabel = fals…`
  - `final String? identifier` — The identifier a tap by identifier reaches this control through — the control's own, or a wrapper's that holds no other control — checked the way replay finds it: the first node on screen with that identifier.
  - `final String? label` — The control's label, its first line, e-mail addresses masked.
  - `final String? tooltip` — The control's tooltip, its first line, masked, when it differs from the label: for the reader of a tape only, since no tap finds a control by it.
  - `final String? within` — The nearest identifier above a control that a tap by identifier does not reach — the row a chip sits in.
  - `final String role` — `button`, `tab`, `textField`, `menuItem` or `other`.
  - `final String? action` — What a click does: `tap`, `expand` or `collapse` ([activationOf]); null when nothing under the point takes a click.
  - `final Rect? rect` — The control's rect on the view, in logical pixels.
  - `final bool reachedByLabel` — Whether a tap by [label] reaches this control — the first tappable node on screen with that label, as a tap by label takes it; false for a second *Cancel* behind the first.
  - `bool get resolved` — Whether replay can reach the control: by its identifier or its label.
- **function** `SemanticsHit? semanticsNodeAt(SemanticsNode root, Offset point, double devicePixelRatio)` — The control a click at [point] (logical pixels of the view) reaches, named the way replay acts on it (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-Issue Recorder.md` §3.2): the node drawn on top at the point — the last in walk order whose…
- **function** `SemanticsNode? findById(SemanticsNode root, int id)` — The node whose id is [id] under [root], or null.
- **function** `SemanticsHit describeControl(SemanticsNode root, SemanticsNode hit, double devicePixelRatio)` — [hit] — the node drawn at a point, or the node a screen reader acted on — named the way replay reaches it:
- **function** `String? focusedTextIdentifier(SemanticsNode root)` — The identifier of the text field that has the focus, when its value travels ([valueIdentifiers]); null otherwise.

### `lib/src/settings_provider.dart`

- **variable** `final sharedPreferencesProvider = Provider<SharedPreferencesWithCache?>((ref)` — The preference store, supplied by `main`.
- **variable** `final developmentModeDefaultProvider = Provider<bool>((ref)` — Whether development mode is on before anyone has chosen (§9.5): on wherever the build has the switch.
- **class `RecentProject`** — A project folder the user opened before, for the sidebar menu.
  - `const RecentProject({required this.path, required this.name})`
  - `final String path`
  - `final String name` — The film's name when it was last opened, else the folder name.
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()`
  - `static RecentProject? fromJson(Object? json)` — Null for anything that is not a `{path, name}` object, so an unreadable entry is dropped rather than crashing the settings.
- **class `Settings`** — User preferences.
  - `const Settings({ this.themeMode = ThemeMode.system, this.viewerHandle = '', this.sidebarWidth = defaultSidebarWidth, this.locale, this.verboseLogs…`
  - `static const double defaultSidebarWidth`
  - `static const int maxRecentProjects` — How many opened folders the menu remembers.
  - `final ThemeMode themeMode`
  - `final String viewerHandle` — The handle whose versions count as "mine" (§6.1 author-first resolution, §13.3 column one).
  - `final double sidebarWidth`
  - `final Locale? locale` — The chosen language, or null to follow the platform.
  - `final bool verboseLogs` — Log at debug level instead of info (`filmopen_store`'s `app_log.dart`).
  - `final List<RecentProject> recentProjects` — Most recent first.
  - `final String? libraryPath` — A shared-library folder chosen by the user, or null for the app's own.
  - `final bool accountSignedIn` — Whether a filmopen.ai session is kept on this machine.
  - `final bool warnInsteadOfRefuse` — Development mode (§9.5): a rule about who may do what warns instead of refusing.
  - `final String? dictationDevice` — The microphone dictation records from (§9.6; milestone 4.9 plan, D8): an id the system gave, or null for the system's default.
  - `final bool dictationHoldToRecord` — Whether holding a box's microphone records while it is held and applies the text on release (§9.6).
  - `final String? dictationEngine` — The speech service dictation transcribes with (§9.6), by the id `filmopen_dictation` gives it, or null for its default.
  - `Guards get guards` — The policy every write of this session applies (`ProjectWriter`).
  - `Author? get viewer` — The viewer, or null: an empty handle, and one that is not a handle (§5.6: `owner[.workspace]`, each a segment; never `official`) — the files are named after it, so an invalid one writes nothing and browses as nobody.
  - `Settings copyWith({ ThemeMode? themeMode, String? viewerHandle, double? sidebarWidth, Locale? locale, bool clearLocale = false, bool? verboseLogs,…`
- **variable** `final settingsProvider`
- **class `SettingsController`**
  - `void setLocale(Locale? locale)` — Null follows the platform language.
  - `void setThemeMode(ThemeMode mode)`
  - `void setViewerHandle(String handle)`
  - `void setSidebarWidth(double width)`
  - `void setVerboseLogs(bool verbose)`
  - `void addRecentProject(String path, String name)` — Puts [path] at the top of the recent list, replacing an older entry for the same folder.
  - `void removeRecentProject(String path)`
  - `void setLibraryPath(String? path)` — Null returns to the app's own library folder.
  - `void setWarnInsteadOfRefuse(bool warn)` — Development mode's switch (§9.5), from Settings → Development.
  - `void setAccountSignedIn(bool signedIn)` — Set by the account card when a session starts or ends (§6.4: the hint is all the preferences file learns of the account).
  - `void setDictationDevice(String? id)` — The microphone dictation records from (§9.6); null returns to the system's default.
  - `void setDictationHoldToRecord(bool hold)` — Dictation's *Hold to record* switch (§9.6).
  - `void setDictationEngine(String? id)` — The speech service dictation transcribes with (§9.6); null returns to the default.

### `lib/src/settings_tab_provider.dart`

  - `static const keys` — Provider keys (§6.7).
  - `static const usage` — Usage: what this device's keys have run up (§6.7; milestone 4.9 plan, D9).
  - `static const plugins` — Plugins (milestone 5.1 plan §3.9).
- **variable** `final settingsTabProvider` — Which of Settings' tabs shows.
- **class `SettingsTabController`** — Holds the index of Settings' tab showing; Settings' bar and the dashboard set it.

### `lib/src/tree_builder.dart`

- **class `TreeBuilder`** — Builds the browsable tree of a project: the script drilled down by folder and scene, what is not in it, then each library and pipeline type, then render batches.
  - `TreeBuilder(this.project, this.l10n, {this.viewer, ScriptOutline? outline})`
  - `final FilmProject project`
  - `final AppLocalizations l10n`
  - `final Author? viewer` — The current user, for author-first resolution of story references.
  - `List<TreeNode> build()`

### `lib/src/tree_node.dart`

- **class `TreeIcon`** — What a row's icon stands for.
  - `const TreeIcon()`
- **class `EntityTreeIcon`** — The icon of an entity type (`iconFor` in the UI package).
  - `const EntityTreeIcon(this.type)`
  - `final EntityType type`
- **class `GlyphTreeIcon`** — A row that is not an entity: a grouping, or a record.
  - `const GlyphTreeIcon(this.glyph)`
  - `final TreeGlyph glyph`
- **enum `TreeGlyph`** — The grouping rows' glyphs.
  - values: `script`, `versions`, `shots`, `cues`, `epoch`, `record`, `other`, `unfiled`, `unread`
- **function** `bool rowHoldsContents(ScriptRow row)` — Whether [row] is where a folder's contents are drawn: the **first** readable row of it, a second listing and a cycle holding nothing (§5.12).
- **class `ScriptPlace`** — Where a row of the script sits (milestone 5.11): what its menu, a drag and an agent's taps act on.
  - `const ScriptPlace({this.parent, this.entry, this.occurrence = 0, this.index, this.siblings, this.container, this.name})`
  - `factory ScriptPlace.ofRow(ScriptRow row)` — Where [row] sits: the list that holds it, the entry as written, and — for a folder that is drawn with what it holds — the version an *Add* goes into.
  - `final Entity? parent` — The file whose `children` lists the row — the project file in use, or the version of the folder drawn above it.
  - `final String? entry` — The entry as the parent writes it, and which of the equal entries it is: what the list's edits take (`withChildRemoved`, `withChildMoved`).
  - `final int occurrence`
  - `final int? index` — Where the entry stands in [parent]'s list, and how long that list is — every entry of a list is a row, readable or not, so a row's place is the entry's — for *Move up* and *Move down* and their ends.
  - `final int? siblings`
  - `final Entity? container` — The file an *Add* here goes into: the project file for the Script row, the version drawn for a folder's row; null for a scene's row and for a row that names nothing.
  - `final String? name` — What a message calls the row: the entity's name, else the entry.
- **class `TreeNode`** — One row of the project tree.
  - `const TreeNode({ required this.id, required this.label, required this.icon, this.detail, this.tooltip, this.shortName, this.place, this.selection,…`
  - `final String id` — Unique within the tree; stable across rebuilds so expansion survives.
  - `final String label`
  - `final String? detail` — Secondary text shown after the label, muted.
  - `final String? tooltip` — Longer explanation shown on hover, when [detail] is not enough.
  - `final String? shortName` — The entity's short name where the row shows it nowhere — a folder's, whose detail is its kind — so that the filter still finds a row *by name or tag*, as its box says.
  - `final ScriptPlace? place` — Where the row sits in the script; null for every row outside it.
  - `final TreeIcon icon`
  - `final Selection? selection` — What clicking the row shows; null for rows that only group.
  - `final List<TreeNode> children`
  - `final bool initiallyExpanded`
  - `final bool isOfficial` — Marked with a star: the version an official pointer names.
  - `final bool isPick` — Marked with a check: the version in use because the viewer picked it (§13.4).
  - `final bool isStalePick` — Shown in red: the project made another version official after the viewer picked this one (§13.2).
  - `final bool hasProblem` — Marked with a warning: an unresolved or ambiguous reference.
  - `bool get hasChildren`
  - `String get searchText` — Text the filter matches against.
- **class `TreeModel`** — The built tree plus an index from selections to rows.
  - `TreeModel(this.roots)`
  - `TreeModel.empty()`
  - `final List<TreeNode> roots`
  - `String? nodeIdFor(Selection selection)` — The row that best represents [selection], or null when the tree has no row for it.
  - `bool contains(String id)` — Whether the tree has a row [id]: a row of the script changes its id when it changes its place.
  - `TreeNode? nodeOf(String id)` — The row [id] as the tree has it **now**, or null: what a drop reads, since the row a drag carries is the one it was picked up as, and the project may have been re-read under it.
  - `List<TreeNode> ancestorsOf(String id)` — Every ancestor row of [id], outermost first; empty when absent.
